newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank - no truth in rumour Tietmeyer to resign.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank - no truth in rumour Tietmeyer to resign.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday that market rumours that Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer had resigned or planned to resign had no basis in fact.
"This rumour has absolutely no basis in fact," a Bundesbank spokeswoman told Reuters in answer to an enquiry.

Dealers said the rumours may have found their origin in various comments that the Bundesbank had had mixed feelings about German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plans to revalue German currency and gold reserves.
The Bundesbank has been discussing this issue at its council meeting on Wednesday and is expected to make a comment later.

Independent analysts have said that Waigel's hastily unveiled plan to revalue reserves could be interpreted as a last-ditch effort to plug the gaping deficit, even as there were various views on whether the funds generated by a revaluation could actually be used to pare the government's deficit in time for currency union.

The fiercely independent Bundesbank is no stranger to conflict with Bonn. Former Bundesbank president Karl Otto Poehl resigned in 1991 in protest at the currency conversion between the east and west German currencies during unification.
The Tietmeyer talk briefly affected the markets with German bonds widening their losses. Losses have however now been pared back after the Bundesbank's official comment on the talk.
